messages.content: Quick update — I finished the retrieval-augmented generation module this week and built a small RAG demo over my own notes.
That's a great milestone. What retrieval strategy did you use — dense embeddings, BM25, or a hybrid approach? And how did you evaluate whether the retrieved chunks were actually relevant?
I used dense embeddings with a simple cosine similarity search, no hybrid yet. For evaluation I mostly eyeballed the outputs — I didn't set up anything systematic.

Eyeballing is a fine start, but for your portfolio you'll want at least a small labeled eval set — even 20 query/expected-chunk pairs — so you can show a retrieval precision number in an interview. Want to add that as your next step?
Yes, let's do that. Also I'm a bit stuck on chunking strategy — my documents are long technical PDFs and naive fixed-size chunking is splitting tables in half.

That's a very common real-world problem. Structure-aware chunking (splitting on headings/sections, keeping tables intact as single chunks) usually solves this better than fixed token windows. Have you tried a layout-aware PDF parser yet, or are you extracting raw text first?

Raw text extraction with pypdf right now, no layout awareness. I'll look into a layout-aware parser. Separately, I wanted to ask about my job search — I've applied to about 8 roles so far and heard back from none of them.

Eight applications with zero responses after a few weeks is worth investigating rather than just applying to more. Can you tell me what roles you're targeting, and whether you're tailoring your resume per application or sending the same one each time?
Mostly generic 'AI Engineer' postings at mid-size companies, and honestly I've been sending the same resume every time without tailoring it.

That's very likely the bottleneck, not your skills. Untailored resumes get filtered by both ATS keyword matching and human reviewers within seconds. Let's fix the RAG eval set this week, then next session we'll rebuild your resume around 2-3 target postings specifically so we can compare before/after.
